methodological_rigor.justification: This study constructs a prognostic gene-expression risk model using TCGA BRCA data (reported 741 samples after preprocessing) with validation in an independent GEO dataset (GSE7390; 198 samples), which is an appropriate framework for hypothesis-generating prognostic modeling (Methods). The modeling pipeline includes DEG identification with FDR control, Cox regression, LASSO feature selection, and time-dependent AUC reporting for both discovery and validation datasets, supporting basic methodological adequacy (Methods; Results). However, the work bundles many secondary analyses (immune deconvolution, drug sensitivity inference, mutation/TMB comparisons) without a clearly prespecified analysis plan, and risks of batch effects, information leakage, and overfitting are not fully addressed in the normalized text (Methods; Results). Overall rigor is competent for an in silico prognostic model but has identifiable gaps in validation depth and causal interpretation.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: The manuscript is an individual cohort-type prognostic modeling study using existing clinical follow-up linked to gene expression (TCGA) with independent validation in another cohort (GSE7390), which aligns best with Oxford LoE 2b for a prognostic/prediction model setting (Methods). The clinical intent (survival prediction via a nomogram incorporating risk score and clinicopathologic features) is relevant to stratification, but the evidence remains observational and computational without prospective evaluation or demonstration of clinical decision impact (Abstract; Results). Experimental validation is limited to RT-qPCR consistency checks for selected genes, which does not establish clinical utility (Abstract; Results).

reporting_quality.justification: This is a prediction/prognostic model paper, so TRIPOD applies; the manuscript reports data sources (TCGA and GEO), sample counts after filtering, core modeling steps (limma with BH-FDR, Cox/LASSO, validation AUCs, nomogram with C-index), and some calibration discussion (Methods; Results). Key TRIPOD details are still incomplete in the normalized text, including full model specification (coefficients), handling of potential batch effects between TCGA and GEO, and a transparent description of missing data handling beyond excluding OS=0/missing survival in GSE7390 (Methods). Data are at least publicly accessible via the named repositories (TCGA, GEO), but no analysis code repository is described, limiting reproducibility of the pipeline (Methods).

novelty_literature.justification: The manuscript proposes an eight-gene HER2-related prognostic risk model with a nomogram and adds immune-microenvironment and drug-sensitivity association analyses (Abstract; Results). Prognostic gene signatures in breast cancer, including HER2-stratified models, are common, and the approach (DEGs, Cox/LASSO, validation AUCs) is a standard template rather than a novel method (Methods). The contribution is therefore incremental unless it demonstrates clear superiority or clinical utility beyond prior signatures.

writing_presentation.justification: The paper is broadly structured and includes a detailed Methods section describing the bioinformatic steps and statistical tests used (Methods). Results are reported with concrete performance numbers (AUCs at 1/3/5 years; C-index) and the limitations section acknowledges sample size and need for mechanistic/drug validation (Results; Discussion). Some statements (for example, causal interpretations about HER2 status and staging) read overstated for observational transcriptomic analyses, and overall prose is occasionally repetitive, but the main workflow is understandable.

key_strengths: Uses a large public discovery cohort (TCGA BRCA; 741 samples reported) with independent validation in a GEO cohort (GSE7390; 198 samples reported).
Applies common high-dimensional modeling steps (BH-FDR for DEGs; Cox/LASSO; time-dependent AUCs) and integrates a nomogram with reported C-index.
Includes some biological/contextual exploration (pathway enrichment; immune deconvolution; mutation/TMB comparisons) to frame the signature.
key_concerns: High risk of overfitting and analytical flexibility given many parallel secondary analyses without clear prespecification, plus limited discussion of batch effects between TCGA and GEO.
TRIPOD-level reporting gaps (full model coefficients and reproducible pipeline details) and no code sharing described.
Drug sensitivity and immunotherapy-response sections rely on inferred in silico scores (pRRophetic, TIDE/IPS) without experimental or clinical validation.
Limited wet-lab validation (RT-qPCR concordance only) and no demonstration of incremental clinical utility over established prognostic tools.
chief_reviewer.rationale: This is a standard-form in silico prognostic signature paper with an external dataset validation, but the novelty is limited and the work needs stronger methodological transparency, batch-effect handling, and validation of claimed therapeutic/immune implications to be publishable even in a lower-tier venue.
